q0243: Fewer operating systems to run and patch = containers (they share the host kernel). VMs each carry a full guest OS.
q0244: Integrity and origin of compiled binaries in production = code signing, verified before the code runs.
q0245: Remove default permissions and grant only what each job needs = least privilege.
q0246: Most like a real outside attacker = unknown environment (black box): no inside information at all.
q0247: Use the company directory for a cloud tool's logins, with no separate passwords = SAML federation (SSO).
q0248: Stolen hashes reused to authenticate without cracking them = pass-the-hash.
q0249: Cut deployment time and cost, with no servers or OS to manage = serverless.
q0250: The order in which systems come back after an outage = DRP (restoration priorities).
q0251: A finished app, nothing on premises, reachable from anywhere = SaaS.
q0252: Outside workers get access while data stays on company systems, and they use their own devices = VDI.
q0253: Teams answering structured questions about their own risks and controls = risk control self-assessment (RCSA).
q0254: Malware from shared files + no slowdown + no failed logins → a quiet remote access Trojan. Cryptojacking always slows machines down.
q0255: Verify data has not changed = hashing (SHA-256). Checksums catch accidental errors; cryptographic hashes catch tampering.
q0256: One person held all the knowledge and left → job rotation (cross-training) prevents single points of knowledge.
q0257: MFA and patching: category = technical, type = preventive.
q0258: Encrypt and authenticate live voice or video streams = SRTP.
q0259: Only users on the internal network were hit, not home users → the attack sits inside the network path (internal DNS poisoning), not on the website.
q0260: Another device handing out internet access that bypasses corporate controls = rogue access point.
q0261: Unapproved software deployed by staff = shadow IT.
q0262: Align two whole security programs = both adopt the same framework (such as NIST CSF). CIS baselines only standardize system settings.
q0263: Logs and reports suspicious activity without blocking it = detective control.
q0264: Detect fraud by moving people between roles = job rotation. Forcing time off = mandatory vacation.
q0265: Restore an entire system including the OS = image backup (bare-metal restore).
q0266: Spoofed certificate identity → the attacker's own private key and a self-signed certificate that no trusted CA vouches for.
q0267: Protect PII using the existing labels and classifications = DLP policies keyed to those labels.
q0268: Did the user's machine actually connect to the phishing site? Check network logs: proxy, DNS and firewall.
q0269: Before patching a VM with a strict uptime SLA, take a snapshot: the fastest way to roll back.
q0270: Wireless trouble after an upgrade + many APs on similar frequencies at high power = channel overlap (interference).
q0271: A payment demand from a vendor you do not use = invoice scam. Always check the vendor database before paying.
q0272: Vendor patches everything (firmware, OS, application) = SaaS. In IaaS you patch the OS and apps; in PaaS you patch your apps.
